data.title: Wall Street Is Unusually Optimistic About Third-Quarter Earnings. Here's Why in 5 Charts. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Elijah Nicholson-Messmer

While it was a mixed week of earnings reports from the big banks, Wall Street analysts still expect big things to come from the third-quarter earnings season that's now under way.

The S&P 500 is expected to report earnings growth of 29.0% for the third quarter — the third straight period of 25%-plus growth. It's an impressive streak, given that the index's earnings have grown at an?average quarterly clip of 12.6% over the past decade, according to FactSet.

The third-quarter growth is likely to head even higher, once companies start reporting, given the typical history of earnings beats from Corporate America.

Already, a historic number of S&P 500 companies have forecast earnings for the quarter above what analysts had expected. Wall Street, in other words, is full of good vibes.

Here are five charts that show how this corporate confidence is breaking out across the index — and where it might be heading.

The 72 companies offering upbeat forecasts is unprecedented, according to FactSet.

"This quarter marks the highest number of S&P 500 companies issuing positive EPS guidance for a quarter since FactSet began tracking this metric in 2006," FactSet Senior Earnings Analyst John Butters wrote in a recent note.

On the other side of things, just 44 companies have offered downbeat guidance — well below the 10-year average of 57.

Stocks in the information technology sector have dominated the strong guidance. The sector accounts for 44 of the 72 total positive preannouncements.

Within tech, software and semiconductor companies are leading the charge. Fueled by seemingly insatiable demand for artificial intelligence, the semiconductor industry alone is projected to grow Q3 earnings by 130% year-over-year.

The strong outlooks from companies are showing up in Wall Street's evolving view of the quarter. While analysts now expect third-quarter earnings growth of 29.0% from S&P 500 companies, on June 1 that forecast was more than two percentage points lower.

Interestingly, the biggest change is being driven by the energy sector, where Wall Street's projected year-over-year growth surged to 128% (up from 79% in June) following a jump in crude oil prices. Tech growth estimates rose to 65%, up eight percentage points from initial estimates at the start of the quarter.

Much of the S&P 500 seems to be finding ways to offset rising costs, resulting in a higher net margin. In fact, S&P 500 net profit margins are expected to reach nearly 15% for Q3 2026, up about two percentage points from the same period last year. That would mark the index's second highest net profit margin since 2009, when FactSet began tracking the metric. Energy and tech, again, lead the expansion. Financials, meanwhile, faced the largest drag.

Analysts say some industries are better able than others to pass higher costs on to customers.

"Resilient demand, especially in manufacturing sectors, likely continued to support companies in passing through higher prices, similar as in Q2," analysts at Deutsche Bank Research wrote in a recent note. "At the same time, consumer conditions remained weak, as retail sales declined further and confidence recovered only modestly."

The earnings tailwind that's been boosting stocks could be peaking, if current estimates hold. Over the next three quarters, Wall Street sees a slowdown, with quarterly growth turning nearly flat by the second quarter of 2027.

Write to Elijah Nicholson-Messmer at elijah.nicholson-messmer@barrons.com

data.title: Mergers and acquisitions
data.description:
The following bids, mergers, acquisitions and disposals were reported by 2005 GMT on Friday:

** SoftBank Group is considering an acquisition of Allied Universal in a deal that could value the US security services provider at about $18 billion, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

** Clothing retailer True Religion is exploring options, including a full sale or minority stake sale that could value the brand, known for its denim, at close to $1 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

** Dulux paint maker AkzoNobel and US peer Axalta Coating Systems have offered remedies in an effort to secure EU antitrust approval for their $25 billion merger, a European Commission filing showed.

** French pasta maker Panzani and Portugal's Cerealis are in exclusive talks to combine their operations in a deal valuing the merged business at about €1.8 billion ($2.03 billion), they said.

** UniCredit , Italy's second-largest bank, said the European Central Bank had authorised it to take control of Commerzbank , after a hostile takeover offer completed in July lifted its stake in the German rival to 48%.

** CCC Intelligent Solutions said it agreed to be acquired by a consortium of private investment firms led by GTCR and including Elliott Investment Management in a $6.1 billion take-private deal.

** Britain's culture minister Lisa Nandy said she would not refer Axel Springer's planned purchase of the Telegraph Media Group to a more detailed competition investigation, clearing the way for the deal to proceed.

** Thoma Bravo-owned cybersecurity company Proofpoint will buy data security firm Varonis Systems in an all-cash deal valued at about $6.3 billion, the companies said.

data.title: Kimbell Royalty Partners Files 8K - Other Events >KRP
data.description:
Kimbell Royalty Partners L.P. (KRP) filed a Form 8K - Other Events - with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission on October 16, 2026.

On October 16, 2026, Kimbell Royalty Partners, LP (the "Partnership") delivered a notice of redemption to the holders of its Series A Cumulative Convertible Preferred Units representing limited partner interests in the Partnership (the "Preferred Units"), which calls for redemption on November 16, 2026 (the "Redemption Date") of 81,250 Preferred Units, representing half of the outstanding Preferred Units as of the date of the notice. The Preferred Units called for redemption will be redeemed on the Redemption Date at a price of $1,233.37895 per Preferred Unit for an aggregate redemption price of approximately $100.2 million. The redemption is expected to be funded with borrowings under the Partnership's revolving credit facility.

This report shall not constitute a notice of redemption with respect to or an offer to purchase or sell (or the solicitation of an offer to purchase or sell) any securities.

Statements in this report that are not historical facts, including but not limited to those relating to the proposed redemption and amounts or proceeds to be used for the redemption, are forward-looking statements that are based on current expectations. Although the Partnership believes that its expectations are based on reasonable assumptions, it can give no assurance that these expectations will prove correct. Important factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those in the forward-looking statements include the terms of the redemption, other sources and uses of funds for the Partnership, actions by the holders of Preferred Units, results of operations, market conditions, capital needs and uses and other risks and uncertainties that are beyond the Partnership's control, including those described in the Partnership's Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 and in its other filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

data.title: Alcon Gets FDA Approval for Brytly Eye Drops
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

Alcon received approval from the Food and Drug Administration for its Brytly eye drops.

The company said Friday that it expects to make Brytly available for retail and online shopping in the coming months following the FDA's decision, with future expansion into additional markets.

Brytly can reduce eye redness for up to 12 hours, up to 50% longer than Bausch + Lomb's Lumify drops, Alcon said.

Write to Elias Schisgall at elias.schisgall@wsj.com

data.title: Rayonier Announces Fourth Quarter 2026 Dividend
data.description:
Rayonier Inc. () announced today that the Company’s board of directors has declared a fourth quarter cash dividend of $0.26 per common share. The dividend is payable on December 31, 2026, to shareholders of record on December 17, 2026.

The Company also announced today that the Company’s board of directors, in its capacity as the board of directors of the general partner of Rayonier, L.P., has declared a fourth quarter cash distribution of $0.26 per operating partnership unit. The cash distribution is payable on December 31, 2026, to holders of record on December 17, 2026.

About Rayonier

Rayonier is a land resources real estate investment trust (REIT) with a portfolio comprising over four million acres in the U.S. South and U.S. Northwest. The company is focused on managing its timberlands on a sustainable basis while optimizing its overall portfolio value by delivering land to its highest and best use. Rayonier also operates six sawmills, an industrial-grade plywood mill, residential and commercial real estate developments, and a rural land sales program. Rayonier is committed to corporate responsibility, third-party forest certification, and supporting climate change mitigation through its land-based solutions business. More information is available at www.rayonier.com.

data.title: Foreign holdings of US Treasuries rise in August; China holdings drop -data
data.description:
Foreign holdings of U.S. Treasuries edged higher in August after two months of declines, data from the Treasury Department showed on Friday, led by gains in holdings from the UK and Canada.

Holdings of U.S. Treasuries rose to $9.331 trillion in August, from $9.248 trillion in the previous month. Compared with a year earlier, Treasuries owned by foreigners were up less than 1%.

China's holdings, however, dropped to $590.7 billion, the lowest since August 2008

data.title: Delek US Holdings to Host Third Quarter 2026 Conference Call on November 6, 2026
data.description:
Delek US Holdings, Inc. () (“Delek US”) today announced that the Company intends to issue a press release summarizing third quarter 2026 results before the U.S. stock market opens on Friday, November 6, 2026. A conference call to discuss these results is scheduled to begin at 10:00 a.m. CT (11:00 a.m. ET) on Friday, November 6, 2026.

The live broadcast of this conference call will be available online by going to www.DelekUS.com and clicking on the investor relations section of the website. A presentation containing supplemental financial information will also be available online at ir.delekus.com prior to the conference call and webcast. The Company does not intend to furnish this presentation on a Current Report on Form 8-K. Investors are encouraged to review the presentation in conjunction with the Company’s earnings press release and webcast. The online replay will be available on the website for 90 days.

About Delek US Holdings, Inc.

Delek US Holdings, Inc. is a diversified downstream energy company with assets in petroleum refining, logistics, pipelines, and renewable fuels. The refining assets consist primarily of refineries operated in Tyler and Big Spring, Texas, El Dorado, Arkansas and Krotz Springs, Louisiana with a combined nameplate crude throughput capacity of 302,000 barrels per day.

The logistics operations include Delek Logistics Partners, LP (). Delek Logistics Partners, LP is a growth-oriented master limited partnership focused on owning and operating midstream energy infrastructure assets. Delek US Holdings, Inc. and its subsidiaries owned approximately 58.0% (including the general partner interest) of Delek Logistics Partners, LP as of September 30, 2026.

Information about Delek US Holdings, Inc. can be found on its website (www.delekus.com), investor relations webpage (ir.delekus.com), and news webpage (www.delekus.com/news).

data.title: ICE review: Canola Weakens on Seasonal Harvest Pressure
data.description:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba--The ICE Futures canola market was weaker on Friday, hitting fresh seven-week lows as steady farmer selling and bearish technical signals weighed on prices.

  • November canola was down by C$2.90 at C$798.80 per ton, with the move below C$800 per ton bearish from a chart standpoint.
  • Losses in the Chicago soy complex and European rapeseed contributed to the softer tone in canola, although Malaysian palm oil was firmer to end the week.
  • Seasonal harvest pressure remained a bearish influence, as warm and dry forecasts across most of the Prairies this weekend should allow farmers to make good progress bringing in the last of the crop.
  • Farmers delivered 620,100 tons of canola into the commercial pipeline during the week ended Oct. 11, reported the Canadian Grain Commission. While that was down by 19% from the previous week, crop-year-to-date deliveries at 4.45 million tons are 28% ahead of last year's pace.
  • Weekly Canadian canola exports at 158,300 tons were down from 248,400 tons the previous week. Crop-year-to-date exports are up 44% on the year at 1.38 million tons through 10 weeks.
  • There were 113,995 contracts traded on Friday, which compares with Thursday when 107,034 contracts changed hands. Spreading accounted for 81,200 of the contracts traded.
